issues.description: Method SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice(Meal): the problem statement (UML and text) specifies calculateTotalPrice should return a double (double precision) and explicitly instructs using double precision for accurate financial calculations. The solution implementation declares public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal) and accumulates/returns an int. This creates a clear return-type mismatch: the problem expects a double result but the solution exposes an int return type. Students and automated graders can be confused about the expected API and numeric precision; if code or tests rely on a double return type this inconsistency can lead to incorrect implementations or failing checks.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature and implementation consistent with the problem statement: change the method declaration in SealSaloon to public static double calculateTotalPrice(Meal meal) and accumulate prices using a double accumulator (e.g., double sum = 0.0; sum += (double) ingredient.getPrice();). Return the double sum. Update any dependent code or tests to expect a double return value and ensure any formatting or comparisons use appropriate double-aware logic.

issues.description: Project/exercise identifier mismatch: the problem statement and UML refer to a 'Seal Saloon' exercise (title: 'H02E02 - Panic at Seal Saloon' and class names like SealSaloon), whereas the template and solution repository metadata declare rootProject.name values referencing 'Panic-at-Burger-House' ('H04E01---Panic-at-Burger-House' in template/settings.gradle and 'H04E01---Panic-at-Burger-House-Solution' in solution/settings.gradle). Students may be confused which project they are working on (Seal Saloon vs Burger House) when the exercise title and repository metadata differ.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical exercise name and align all artifacts. Either update problem_statement.md to use 'Panic-at-Burger-House' and adjust the UML/title accordingly, or (preferable) change both template_repository/settings.gradle and solution_repository/settings.gradle rootProject.name to a Seal Saloon–centric value (for example, 'H02E02---Panic-at-Seal-Saloon' or 'Panic-at-Seal-Saloon' ) so the repository metadata matches the problem statement and UML.
